notes: Last time I stopped at 'Developer mode'. This time 'Keine KI-App? … Mit Ihren Zahlen testen' (landing.txt:231-235) took me to /try. My code worked, and nine short questions later I had my own report, which says 'Von einer KI: nichts' (try-done-report.png). All six of my loop-1 points are fixed. The German talks the way I do: Sie, Z-Bon, Strichliste, an envelope of receipts, '9,90 €', '1.500 €'. Now I see why VAT comes out first: of my 9,90 €, 8,95 € is mine, 5,35 € after ingredients. My calculator agrees: 8 × 5,35 − 36,57 = 6,23, × 10 − 180 = −117,70, so '−118 €' is right (report.txt:298). I would show the facts card to my Steuerberater: § 12 UStG, a date, a link, even 'Milchgetränke … 7 %'. What holds it back: my own report counts 6 numbers from me and '12 Schätzungen' that 'nur Ihr Test kann prüfen'. /try never asked about the sign, an extra staff hour or my spare cash, yet the worst case rests on them. I am told to remember one number (11), but the card keeps the deal at 7. The interview repeats three answers word for word (report.txt:479-511).
improvements: /try and my own report (try-walkthrough.txt screens 1-9; try-done-report.png 'Von Ihnen: 6 Zahlen … Schätzungen: 12. Nur Ihr Test kann sie prüfen'): /try asks for 6 numbers, so the sign and flyers (180 € in the demo), the extra staff hour, the advertising and the money I can spare must be assumed. The worst case and '% des Geldes, das Sie entbehren können' then rest on numbers I never gave. Add three short questions to /try (Startkosten für Schild/Flyer, zusätzliche Personalstunden pro Tag, wie viel Sie ohne Sorgen ausgeben könnten), or list every assumed value on 'Ihre Zahlen prüfen' with a field to change it ('Angenommen: 180 € für Schild und Flyer, ändern'). Label assumed facts 'Angenommen, bitte prüfen', not 'Schätzung, nur Ihr Test kann sie prüfen': no test will tell me my spare cash. Criterion: would she use it for a real decision. It worked when every number behind the worst-case bar and the cash stop line in a /try report is one she typed or confirmed.

One number or two? The landing says 'Die eine Zahl, die Sie sich merken … Gewinnschwelle: 11 pro Tag' (landing.txt:138-142). Step 4 is called 'Die Zahl zum Merken' but shows 11 and 7. The test card keeps the deal at 7 (report.txt:547-552), and 'Was Sie gelernt haben' ends with 'nach dem Test zählen nur die 7 pro Tag' (report.txt:568). Say it the same way everywhere: 'Zwei Zahlen: 11, damit sich der Test bezahlt macht; 7, damit sich das Angebot danach trägt. Für Ihre Entscheidung zählt die 7.' Put both numbers in the short-answer card, and change the landing tile and the Step 4 heading to match. Criterion: owner understanding. It worked when Selin, asked 'at how many do you keep it?', answers 7 without hesitating, and nothing anywhere calls 11 'the one number'.

Step 5 interview (report.txt:476-511): six answers but only three texts. Chiara = Paweł, Noor = Greta and Murat = Jan, word for word. The German also slips: 'komme ich weiter' (report.txt:499, 511) means 'I am making progress', and 'Kommt weiter für das Angebot' (report.txt:439) is not how anyone talks. Group identical answers ('2 Gäste sagten: …') or vary them, and write 'komme ich gern wieder' and 'Kommt weiterhin wegen des Angebots'. Criterion: the rehearsal feels like a neighbourhood, not a template. It worked when no two names show the same sentence and a German reader finds nothing odd in Step 5.

Guess labels that don't agree. Step 1 says 'Schätzungen: 5' (report.txt:59). Step 6 says 'Alle 4 Schätzungen vergleichen' and lists 'Was ein Mittagsgast heute ausgibt' and 'Zutaten pro Angebot', which Step 2 shows as my numbers (report.txt:134-135, 528-539). The VAT mix sits under 'Ihr Test prüft sie' (report.txt:114-117), but only my Steuerberater can check it. Call the Step 6 chart 'Welche Zahl bewegt das Ergebnis am meisten (Ihre Zahlen und Schätzungen)', and give the VAT mix its own note: 'prüft Ihre Steuerberatung, nicht der Test'. Criterion: knowing what is mine, what is a guess and what is a fact. It worked when every count and list of 'Schätzungen' in the report names the same items.

It worked when report.txt for a /try report has no 'Coach' and no contradicting counts.
understood: Break-even in my words: with the 180 € sign and flyers, I need 11 more lunch guests every weekday for the 10-day test to pay for itself. If I keep the deal afterwards, 7 a day is enough, because the sign is paid either way.

The most the test could cost me: −546 € if nobody new comes and 3 in 10 of my lunch regulars switch. That is 36 % of the 1.500 € I could spare. It could reach −862 € if all of them switched. The cash out of my envelope is about 295 € by day 5 and 410 € over 10 days.
The guess that matters most is how many extra guests come: 3 or 15 a day changes the result by 642 €, so that is what I count.
VAT is not mine: of 9,90 €, 8,95 € stays with me after 10,6 % VAT, and 5,35 € after ingredients. A regular's usual 11,20 € lunch leaves me 6,54 €, so every regular who switches costs me 1,19 €.

The test card: one normal week of counting lunch guests first, a deal button on the till, a tally sheet with 'neu' and 'isst sonst auch mittags hier', receipts in an envelope, stop on day 5 if I average under 4 a day.
The six customers are made up and played by fixed rules, not an AI. They give me questions to ask real guests (vegetarian every day? swap the drink for a coffee?), never numbers.

wouldTry: yes, because I can start on Monday with the one-week baseline count on a tally sheet by the till. The card tells me what to count, when to stop (day 5, under 4 a day, about 295 € of receipts) and when to keep it (7 a day). Before I spend 180 € on a sign, I would want my own sign cost, staff hour and spare cash in /try. It never asked me for them.
learnedAboutAI: Plain code did all 24 sums, and I can open each one and redo it. My calculator agreed on −117,70 €. The extra guests and the 30 % of regulars switching are guesses that only my test can answer. The six customers were made up and played by fixed rules with no AI. They are good for questions and never a count. In my own /try report the AI did nothing at all. With Claude connected, the AI would ask the questions and play the customers, but never do the money. What I take with me: when an AI gives me a number, ask whether it is mine, calculated, guessed or imagined.
germanFirst: It reads like a person wrote it for a café owner: 'Sie', short sentences, 'Z-Bon', 'Strichliste neben der Kasse', 'Sammeln Sie die Belege … in einem Umschlag', 'Die Mehrwertsteuer gehört nicht Ihnen'. Numbers are all German ('9,90 €', '1.500 €', '16.500 €', '0,8 %'). Awkward: 'komme ich weiter' (report.txt:499, 511), 'Kommt weiter für das Angebot' (report.txt:439), 'ein zusätzliches Paar Hände' (Step 2 details), 'Teilen Sie ihn also wie eine Tabelle' (report.txt:604). Mixed spelling: 'falschzuliegen' and 'falsch zu liegen'. I never needed the English.
